title: Press module: one place decides what a pointerdown means
lede: Before this PR, the rule that pressing anywhere else ends **Editing** had to be reported from five places (the Note body, the Resize handles, the ×, `focusNote`, empty Board), and two more modules each listened on the whole page. #51 was one of those places forgetting the rule. Now one **Press module** in `src/press/` owns everything that happens when the pointer goes down. Its pure core, `createPress`, decides. Its DOM side, `pressDom.ts`, reads the **Press target** off `data-press-target` attributes and does what the core says. `Note.tsx` keeps only markup and keys.

files.question: What does a press mean?
files.summary: The pure core. It takes a Press target with a pointer, focus on a Note, a click on a ×, the browser's double-click and the Drag controller's Click, and calls the stores and the one Drag controller.
files.owns: Raise, ending Editing, a press inside text, Drag or Click, the Click's caret, creating a Note on double-click, the ignore window after a ×, ending a Drag whose Note was deleted.
files.never: Touches the DOM: it gets plain targets and pointers, and returns what to do with the event (`drag`, `prevent`, `none`).
files.tested: `src/press/press.test.ts`: every rule, in Node, with `createStores()`, the real Drag controller and a fake `DragIO`.

files.question: How do DOM events reach the core?
files.summary: Attached once by the Board. It holds the only `document` listener (`pointerdown`, capture phase) and `focusin`, `click` and `dblclick` on the Board, and builds the real `DragIO` for the one Drag controller.
files.owns: Reading the Press target from `data-press-target`, `data-note-id` and `data-handle`; `preventDefault`; pointer capture; the Preview and the Trash zone look; measuring the Click's caret.
files.never: Decides anything the core decides: no Raise, no Editing, no timing.
files.tested: The browser tests (`editing`, `delete`, `drag`, `keyboard`, `trash`, `board`, `colours`, `App`). `isInText` also has a Node test in `pressDom.test.ts`.

files.question: What is left in a Note?
files.summary: Markup with `data-press-target` on the article (`body`), the Grip strip (`grip`) and the × (`delete`); Enter, Delete, Backspace and Escape; the editor placing the caret Editing carries.
files.owns: Rendering a Note and its keys.
files.never: Listens for `pointerdown` or `focus`, or holds Board DOM references.
files.tested: The browser tests, unchanged except one import line in three files.

files.question: Who attaches the Press module?
files.summary: One effect calls `attachPress` and returns its cleanup. `lastTwoPresses`, `onDoubleClick` and `onPointerDown` are gone.
files.owns: Rendering the Board and its Notes, and attaching the Press module once.
files.tested: The browser tests; `App.browser.test.tsx` covers the double-click cases.

files.question: What changed in the Drag controller?
files.summary: Only the Raise left: `press` no longer calls `kind.press` and has no `inText` option. There is now one controller per Board, not one per Note.
files.owns: The session: Dead zone, Preview, Trash zone, Click, release and cancel.
files.tested: `src/drag/controller.test.ts`: the first test now checks a press saves nothing and only starts listening.

files.question: Where does the Click's caret go?
files.summary: Editing state now carries `caret`, set by `startEditing(id, caret)`. The editor reads it once when it mounts. Enter passes `null`, the end of the text.
files.tested: `src/ui/uiStore.test.ts`: `Editing carries the caret it started with, the end of the text by default`.

scenarios.name: Click an idle Note's text: Editing starts with the caret there

steps.title: The Board attaches the Press module once
steps.explain: One effect, on mount. Its cleanup removes every listener and disposes the core, which cancels a running Drag. Under StrictMode it runs twice, and the second attach starts clean.

steps.title: pointerdown on the text: the DOM side reads the Press target
steps.explain: Captured on `document`, so it runs before anything else. The text has no `data-press-target`, so the nearest marked element is the article: `{ on: 'body', id }`. It passes the plain pointer fields to the core.

run.from: function pressTargetOf(target: EventTarget | null, board: HTMLElement): PressTarget {
run.to: return on === 'grip' || on === 'delete' ? { on, id } : { on: 'body', id };

steps.title: The core: end Editing elsewhere, Raise, hand the Press to the Drag controller
steps.explain: First it records whether this press was on empty Board, for the double-click. Then it reports the press to Editing (any button), checks it is a left-button Press, Raises, and starts the Drag session. It remembers `pressedId` for the Click. The controller's `press` no longer calls `kind.press` or takes `inText`: it ends any earlier session and starts listening, nothing else.

run.to: const pressPoint = { x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY };

steps.title: Back in the DOM side: preventDefault and pointer capture
steps.explain: `drag` means: no focus change, no text selection, and capture the pointer. For a Resize handle, capture goes on the handle so its cursor stays; otherwise on the Note. The Note is remembered as the Preview element.

steps.title: pointerup inside the Dead zone: the controller reports a Click
steps.explain: The controller is unchanged here. Its `io.click` is the DOM side's, which measures the caret on the idle text and hands it to the core. The core starts Editing on the Note it remembered, with that caret.

run.to: return { ...end(state, 'press'), editingId: id, editingEndedBy: null, caret };

steps.title: The editor mounts and places the caret
steps.explain: Read once, before paint. Before this PR the caret was a ref inside `Note`; now it is part of Editing, so Enter (`null`) and a Click go through the same path.

scenarios.name: Note A is in Editing; press inside its text, then on Note B's ×

steps.title: Inside A's textarea: only a Raise
steps.explain: `isInText` is true, so the core reports the press (A is the edited Note, so nothing ends), Raises, and returns `none`: no `preventDefault`, so the caret and selection stay the browser's. The test `inside text only Raises` covers it.

steps.title: On B's ×: Editing ends, but it is no Press
steps.explain: The core reports `pressed(b)` before it looks at the target kind, so a new Press target can't skip it: that is the #51 bug made impossible. Then `delete` returns `prevent`: no Raise, no Drag, and focus stays put.

scenarios.name: Double-click B's ×, with Note A underneath

steps.title: The first click deletes B and opens the ignore window
steps.explain: The DOM side's `click` listener sees a click inside a `delete` target. `detail > 0` means a mouse click, which may be half a double-click, so the core ignores presses on Notes for `DOUBLE_CLICK_MS`.

steps.title: The second press lands on A: ignored
steps.explain: `prevent`, before anything else on a Note: no Raise, no Editing change, no Drag. `preventDefault` on `pointerdown` also suppresses the compatibility `mousedown`. A press on empty Board in the window still works, as it returns earlier. The browser test `a double-click on the × deletes only that Note` checks A is unchanged.

steps.title: Enter on a × in that window still deletes
steps.explain: A change from `ignorePressesFor`, which swallowed every `click` on a Note. A keyboard click (`detail` 0) can't be half a double-click, so only mouse clicks are ignored. The old browser test passed only because its fake timers closed the window early; the core test `clicked from the keyboard during that time still deletes` now proves it directly.

steps.title: Each pointerdown records whether it was on empty Board
steps.explain: On `document`, so a press outside the Board counts as not on empty Board. A `dblclick` only reports where the second press landed, so the first has to be remembered.

steps.title: dblclick: create only if both presses were on empty Board
steps.explain: The DOM side measures the point and the Board's size; the core decides. The core test `whose first press was outside the Board creates nothing` covers the case where nothing should happen.

scenarios.name: Tab to a Note, then Delete it while another is held mid-Drag

steps.title: focusin: keyboard focus Raises, a right-click's focus does not
steps.explain: `:focus-visible` is read in the DOM and passed as `keyboard`. Focus in the textarea does nothing, since only Editing focuses it.

steps.title: A held Note is deleted: its Drag ends at once
steps.explain: Before, each Note had its own controller, cancelled when the Note unmounted. With one controller per Board, the core follows the Notes store instead: when the held Note disappears it disposes the session, which saves nothing, so Undo brings the Note back where it was. Found in review; the core test `whose Note is deleted mid-Drag ends the Drag at once` covers it.

notes.title: Browser tests: one import line changed in three files
notes.detail: The issue asked for them to pass unchanged. `DOUBLE_CLICK_MS` lived in the deleted `ignorePressesFor.ts`; `delete`, `editing` and `keyboard` now import it from `./press/press`. No test body changed.

notes.title: `dblclick`, not `click` with `detail === 2`
notes.detail: The issue lists `focusin` and `click` on the Board. A `dblclick` listener keeps the browser's own double-click timing and matches the old `onDoubleClick`; the core still decides from the two remembered presses.

notes.title: The left-button check lives in the core
notes.detail: The issue moves `isPress` to `pressDom.ts`. It is inline in the core instead, so "only a left-button Press Raises" is tested in Node. `isInText` is in `pressDom.ts`, as asked.

notes.title: Counter-argument: `pressDom.ts` does two jobs
notes.detail: It reads Press targets and it is the Drag controller's real `DragIO`. They share the pressed Note (Preview element, capture, Click caret), which is why they stayed together.

notes.title: Known leftover: the caret after a remount
notes.detail: Editing's `caret` stays set while Editing lasts. If the editor remounted mid-Editing, it would put the caret back at the Click's offset. Nothing remounts it today. Not run.

notes.detail: I didn't click through this walkthrough in a browser; please do. The builder checked that every highlighted line exists.
